correctness.rationale: The l1 reverse triangle inequality gives exact nearest-point characterization. The canonical soft threshold is a selection. Its finite polyhedral derivative matrices are signed centering matrices with exact l1 norm 2-2/k, and finite-segment integration gives the upper bound. For every other selector a common exterior point and n boundary fixed points force a zero-sum displacement q. Convex averaging under n-1 coordinate permutations reduces its Lipschitz obstruction to min_{a in R} max(2|a|, exact l1 distance), whose minimum is 2-2/n. The infinite-index case follows by finite-support restriction and canonical-selector truncations. All dimension/radius boundaries were checked. A separately executed exact rational checker returned L1_METRIC_SELECTION_SHARP_OK 10589; these finite tests do not substitute for the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A set-valued nearest-point mapping in a prototypical nonsmooth Banach space has many selectors; identifying the smallest possible global Lipschitz constant over the whole class is a natural, previously unsettled (best-knowledge) quantitative selection problem. The exact values classify every finite dimension and any infinite index set, show a sharp nonexpansivity threshold at dimension two, and prove that no nonlinear/asymmetric selection can improve the explicit soft-threshold map. The geometric simplex lower bound is substantive beyond routine formula evaluation.
